headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Airflow-to-pdf.js file handoff; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can move data through APIs and broad network egress, while pdf.js reads PDF files and runs browser-based tests. A plausible pairwise pathway is Airflow-generated content being written into PDFs or files that pdf.js then opens, creating an instruction-smuggling risk. The shared channel is inferred, not documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Airflow writes attacker-controlled text into a PDF or file that pdf.js opens
IF pdf.js processes that file as trusted document content without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance labels to files before pdf.js opens them
Restrict Airflow outputs to non-executable templates
Scan PDFs for embedded scripts or suspicious annotations
Open only files from a quarantined staging directory
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and provenance validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and pdf.js touches PDF documents and files. If Airflow passes sensitive file contents into PDFs or adjacent artifacts, pdf.js can expose that content during rendering or testing. No shared workspace is documented, but the file-based pathway is plausible enough to exceed low severity.
conditions: IF Airflow stages sensitive data into files that pdf.js reads
IF those files are accessible outside a restricted workspace
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of shared directories
Redact sensitive fields before Airflow exports files
Use separate service accounts and storage buckets
Review pdf.js test artifacts for embedded document contents
requires-engineering: add access controls and retention rules on shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while pdf.js supports multiple instances and browser-based tests but no write or OAuth scopes are documented. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so a write-write conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an unusual shared filesystem or orchestrator setup, keeping this low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared artifacts
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared outputs
Use file locks on any shared artifact
Run pdf.js in a read-only workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate or transform artifacts, and pdf.js renders PDF documents. If pdf.js consumes Airflow-produced files as authoritative without verification, an upstream mistake can cascade into incorrect rendering or downstream decisions. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows but not proven high-risk.
conditions: IF pdf.js treats Airflow-produced PDFs as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks file integrity or source before rendering
mitigations: Insert checksum verification before pdf.js ingestion
Require a human review step for generated PDFs
Tag generated files as untrusted until validated
Compare rendered output against source metadata
requires-engineering: add explicit trust-boundary enforcement

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is a data-engineering orchestrator and pdf.js processes PDF documents; the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or residency constraints. Because no sensitive regulated data class is documented, a compliance breach is not established. The only plausible issue is generic retention or logging mismatch, which stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Airflow into PDF artifacts
IF retention or logging policies differ for those artifacts
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Set short retention on generated PDFs
Disable verbose logging for document contents
Document data residency for any shared storage
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
